# @arki/pubsub

> Publish and subscribe on named channels over memory, a polled table (Postgres or SQLite), Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY and Redis. Best effort, like NOTIFY. Not a queue.

## Import paths

<!-- llms:start -->
- `@arki/pubsub`: the contract, its limits and its errors. `CHANNEL_PATTERN`, `MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES`, `PUBSUB_ERROR_CODES`, `PubSubError`; types `OnMessage`, `PubSub`, `PubSubErrorCode`, `TransactionalPubSub`, `Unsubscribe`.
- `@arki/pubsub/memory`: in-process fan-out, for tests and one-process apps. `memoryPubSub`.
- `@arki/pubsub/pg`: Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY. `pgPubSub`; types `PgPubSubOptions`, `PgPubSubPool`, `PgTransaction`.
- `@arki/pubsub/poll`: messages in a database table, read by polling. `pollPubSub`, `pubsubTable`; types `PgPollDb`, `PollPubSubOptions`, `PubsubRow`, `PubsubTable`, `SqlitePollDb`.
- `@arki/pubsub/redis`: Redis `PUBLISH`, and `SUBSCRIBE` on a second connection (`client.duplicate()`), since a subscribed Redis connection can run nothing else. `redisPubSub`; types `RedisPubSubOptions`.
- `@arki/pubsub/testing`: the conformance suite every backend runs. `describePubSubContract`; types `PubSubContractOptions`, `PubSubSubject`, `TransactionalPubSubSubject`.
<!-- llms:end -->

## Rules that bite
- Only `pollPubSub` and `pgPubSub` have `publishIn`; it sends at commit and never after a rollback.
- Channels are `^[a-z0-9_]{1,63}$`; payloads are at most 7999 UTF-8 bytes. Send ids.
- `pgPubSub` needs a session pool, never a transaction pooler.
- `close()` never closes your database, pool or Redis client.
